newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL project aimed at moving more heavy oil.
newsitem.headline: IPL project aimed at moving more heavy oil.

text.p: A four-year, C$875 million expansion of IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial Pipe Line is aimed at providing more transport capacity for growing Canadian heavy oil production into the U.S. Midwest, company officials said on Thursday.
Interprovincial earlier announced a staged expansion of its pipeline system that would add 520,000 barrels per day of capacity by 2001.

The plan was in response to a new consensus of oil industry forecasts that shows Canadian light, heavy, synthetic, and bitumen supply is expected to rise by 350,000 barrels per day by 2005 from the current level of about 2.2 million barrels per day, IPL said.

"The majority of this crude is heavy crude that's fueling the growth and the ability to carry heavier slates of crude is important to western Canadian shippers," Interprovincial chief executive Pat Daniel told a media briefing.

IPL figures show heavy oil production, mostly from northeast Alberta, was expected to rise by 500,000 barrels per day over the next eight years. Total production was offset by an expected decline in conventional light oil output.

IPL Energy chief executive Brian MacNeill said the expansion, which would start in 1998 on the heels of its most recent project expected to be begin later this year, was being staged so the company and its shippers could reassess supply and demand forecasts along the way.
"We don't want to over-commit pipeline capacity, but we do want to have a plan that addresses everything that is shown on the current forecast," MacNeill said.

IPL executives said forecasts prepared over the last 10 years have consistently underestimated Canadian crude supply growth, which has resulted in several lengthy periods when apportionment of IPL capacity has been a major headache for producers and refiners.
Canadian firms have announced C$6 billion worth of northeast Alberta heavy oil and oil sands projects which are expected to come on stream over the next 10 years.

Companies such as Interprovincial, Shell Canada Ltd and Suncor Inc have said they were planning pipelines from the region to feed into major export lines. Alberta Energy Co Ltd on Wednesday added its name to the list.

"What we are looking at is a supply forecast that we think is well matched to the market. However, we are going to have to be aggressive in the market place going forward to ensure that we can extend further south from the current markets in Chicago," Daniel said.

Last year, IPL took a stake in the Mustang pipeline to Wood River and Patoka in southern Illinois from Chicago. It is also negotiating with British Petroleum Co Plc to build a 150,000 barrel per day line to its refinery in Toledo, Ohio.

Daniel said he agreed Canadian heavy oil producers faced stiff competition in the Chicago market from offshore suppliers such as Venezuela. However, Canada's low-cost production and the ability to cheaply add transport capacity worked in their favor, he said.
Of the total investment, C$650 million would be spent adding capacity to cure bottlenecks in Canada and the rest in the United States by affiliated Lakehead Pipe Line Partners LP, IPL said.
The company also said it would apply to Canada's National Energy Board within the next 10 days for a C$10 million project to install heaters and modify pumps in Canada.
The project is to allow easier shipment of heavier slates of crude to the U.S. Midwest.
